findings.title: The /channel bind mount lets a guest plant a symlink the host later dereferences, breaking the sandbox boundary
findings.location: packages/@ezcorp/extension-runner/src/podman.ts:142-153 (launchDetached: mkdir mode 0o700 then chmod 0o777 at line 145), :161-186 (channelTransport, unguarded open() at line 163), :196 (args(): the only ro=false mount any guest receives), :342 (attach() calling channelTransport unconditionally on every recovery)
findings.description: The per-attempt channel directory is created 0o700 then immediately widened to 0o777 and bind-mounted into the guest read-write (the only rw mount any guest gets; the pre-existing /workspace mount stays ro=true and is immune). channelTransport() reopens in/out/err by path with plain fs/promises open(), with no lstat/file-type check, on both initial launch and every attach()/recovery. Because the DIRECTORY (not just the FIFOs' own mode bits) is guest-writable, and unlinkat/symlinkat are both permitted by the shipped seccomp allow-list, a guest can unlink a channel entry and replace it with a symlink to an arbitrary absolute host path. I built and ran a live PoC (see poc_evidence below) reproducing the exact mount/permission/security-flag configuration shipped in podman.ts: an unprivileged, fully sandboxed container (cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only rootfs, network=none, user=65534:65534 remapped by rootless Podman to subordinate UID 231069) replaced /channel/out with a symlink to a file outside any container, and a plain host-side open(path,'r') -- exactly what channelTransport() does -- read the planted host file's content instead of the guest's own stream. This is unconditionally reachable via attach()/recovery (not a timing race): an already-running guest can hold arbitrary code execution for an unbounded time before any supervisor reattaches. This directly violates the 'no secret reachable by a guest' security-posture requirement and is a new attack surface introduced by this exact delta (the superseded podman-attach mechanism had no writable host directory mounted into the guest at all).
findings.poc_evidence: /tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w01-revalidation/logs/symlink-swap-poc.md (full commands, exact output, independently authored and run in a scratch directory outside any worktree)
remediation_options: Bind-mount the three FIFO files individually (type=bind,src=<dir>/in,dst=/channel/in, x3) so the guest can read/write FIFO data via already-open descriptors but cannot unlink/rename a directory entry it lacks directory-level write access to.
lstat() each path in channelTransport() and reject if it is not still the expected FIFO before open()-ing it, on every call including reattach.

Do not widen the leaf directory to 0o777; resolve the guest's actual rootless-Podman subordinate-mapped UID/GID and chown/chmod the three FIFO files precisely to that identity instead of loosening the containing directory for 'other'.

item_b_sigkill_test_review.main_test: packages/@ezcorp/extension-runner/tests/podman.integration.test.ts:86-111 is state-driven: starts a real child supervisor, waits for its own 'READY' stdout line (no fixed sleep), SIGKILLs it and awaits child.exited (an observed fact), THEN constructs a fresh supervisor and asserts inspect() reports 'running' strictly before any attach() call.
item_b_sigkill_test_review.controlled_fault_variant: podman.integration.test.ts:113-146 does not exercise PodmanRunner at all; it independently reproduces the superseded mechanism (raw podman run --detach -i + podman attach holding stdin) against a throwaway container, confirms running before killing the holder, then polls the container's own state (bounded 120 attempts, no fixed sleep) until terminal and asserts exit code 7 (the guest's own end-of-input handler). Read the fault injection: it is a faithful, deterministic reproduction of the pre-fix architecture, not a mock. Because it never calls into podman.ts, there is no meaningful 'revert-and-rerun' experiment against it -- it characterizes real Podman's stdin-forwarding behavior, the causal mechanism the design record cites, and it passed deterministically in both of my reruns. Paired with the main test (which proves the NEW mechanism survives the identical kill), this constitutes a genuine A/B causality proof. Considered fully satisfied.
